How well does GroundedMed do?

We tested it once on PubMedQA research questions it was never tuned on, and report every result as measured.

Test questions (PubMedQA, frozen)200S7
Systems tested on2026-10-25S4,S5,S6
Scored on2026-10-26S8
Code version498b76aS9

1. Reading the abstracts is what makes the answers good

Share of the 200S10 test questions answered correctly (PubMedQA's own yes / no / maybe answers; a refusal counts as wrong).

Baseline (reads abstracts)76.5%S11153/200S12
Agent (reads abstracts)74.0%S13148/200S14
Closed-book (same AI, no abstracts)54.0%S15108/200S16

+22.5 ptsS17 baseline vs closed-book (95% range +15.0 to +29.5S18)

+20.0 ptsS19 agent vs closed-book (95% range +12.5 to +27.0S20)

Without the abstracts, the AI did no better than always answering "yes" (55.0%S21). Both gains are well clear of zero.

2. Agent vs baseline: a measured tradeoff

The agent adds a planner and a checker on top of the baseline. On the same 200S22 questions, it produced answers that an independent AI judge more often found fully backed by the cited abstracts, and paid for that in accuracy, time and cost.

What the agent gained

  • Limitations fully supported: 91.3%S23 vs 86.2%S24: +5.1 ptsS25 (95% range +1.8 to +8.6S26; clear)
  • Findings fully supported: 95.0%S27 vs 93.2%S28: +1.8 ptsS29 (95% range −0.04 to +3.7S30; borderline)
  • Answers with any item not fully supported: 40/192S31 (20.8%S32) vs 70/197S33 (35.5%S34)

What it cost

  • Accuracy: 74.0%S35 vs 76.5%S36: −2.5 ptsS37 (95% range −5.0 to −0.5S38), mainly because it declined more questions (coverage 95.0%S39 vs 97.5%S40). When both answered: −0.6 ptsS41, no clear difference.
  • Time: typical answer 11.79 sS42 vs 4.23 sS43
  • AI cost per question: $0.0287S44 vs $0.0131S45

The support figures are one AI judge's estimate. In the second-AI cross-check below, the second AI agreed with the judge less often on the agent's accepted findings (6/10S46) than on the baseline's (8/10S47), on a small sample, so treat the gain as an estimate.

Are the findings backed by their sources? AI-judge estimate

Not the same thing as the accuracy above. An independent AI judge (gemini-3.1-pro-previewS111, Google; not the AI that writes the answers) read each finding with the abstract it cites and labelled it fully, partly or not supported. We report fully supported only.

The agent's checker removes some items and it refuses more, so the two systems are judged on different numbers of items. The findings difference is borderline: its range only just touches 0.

Second-AI cross-check

To test the judge, a second AI from a different company (ChatGPT, OpenAI) labelled a blind sample of 30S1,S2 of the same items without seeing the judge's labels. It agreed with the judge on 14/20S130 = 70.0%S131 (95%: 48.1–85.5%S132) of the items the judge accepted, and on 8/10S133 = 80.0%S134 (95%: 49.0–94.3%S135) of the items the judge rejected. It rejected some items the judge had accepted, which suggests the judge's figures may be optimistic. No person checked these items.

How we tested

  • 200S136 test questions were frozen (IDs and hash) before any system was built and never used for tuning; each system ran on them exactly once.
  • Baseline = search + one AI answer. Agent = planner → search → answer → checker. Closed-book = the AI alone, no abstracts.
  • Ranges: Wilson 95% for percentages; bootstrap for time and cost; differences use a paired bootstrap over the same questions (2000S137 resamples).
  • All figures are produced by the evaluation code and shown here unchanged (rounded to one decimal).

Limitations

  • PubMedQA questions are often written from the article's title, so finding the right abstract is easier than real-world search. We left titles out of the searchable text and added 1,500S3 similar-topic abstracts as distractors, but Hit@5 is still 100.0%S138.
  • PubMedQA has no sentence-level labels showing which sentence supports an answer, so "supported" is judged by AI, not checked against human annotations.
  • The claim-support judge is an AI (a preview model) and was cross-checked only by another AI on 30S1,S2 items.
  • One run per system on 200S139 questions: small differences are within the ranges shown.
  • PubMedQA is public, so the AI may have seen it in training; the closed-book result measures this.
  • Times are from a developer laptop; costs exclude search and reranking.
